narrative:
The model determined that you have a 39% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses for approval, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the status of your checking account, the purpose of the loan, and the presence of a co-applicant. Your checking account currently shows no balance, which is the most influential piece of information. Among approved applicants this situation is actually quite common (59%), yet in your specific combination of details the model interpreted the empty account as a meaningful risk signal that pushed the prediction toward denial.

The fact that you are requesting the loan to buy a new car worked against you as the second-most important factor. While many people finance cars, the model saw this purpose as increasing risk compared with other uses such as home-related purchases that more often receive approval.

Having a co-applicant added a smaller but still noticeable push toward the “bad credit risk” side. Most successful applicants (88%) apply alone; the model appears to treat a co-applicant as an extra layer of complexity that slightly raises concern.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed several positive signals such as your long employment, modest loan amount, and stable housing. 

What you should do next is improve the status of your checking account so it regularly shows funds, then reapply in a few months. This single change tends to have the largest positive effect on similar applications.
